scheme_name: PMMSY: Ice Plant/Cold Store of Minimum 30-Ton Capacity - Haryana
description:
The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) is a flagship scheme launched by the Government of India on September 10, 2020. 

This scheme aims to bring about the holistic development of the fisheries sector in India. 

The PMMSY aims to enhance fish production and productivity in the country. 

One of the specific components of PMMSY is the establishment of ice plants and cold storage facilities. 

The minimum capacity for these facilities is set at 30 tons. 

This initiative is particularly significant for states like Haryana which have a growing demand for fishery products. 

The primary objective of this component is to reduce post-harvest losses in the fishery sector. 

Post-harvest losses can be as high as 20 to 30 percent in the absence of proper storage facilities. 

By establishing ice plants and cold storage, the government aims to ensure better preservation of fish. 

This will ultimately lead to increased income for fish farmers and fishers. 

The scheme also aims to create employment opportunities in the fisheries sector. 

The targeted beneficiaries include fish farmers, fishers, and entrepreneurs involved in the fishery sector. 

The financial assistance provided under this scheme is substantial. 

The government provides a subsidy of up to 40 percent of the total project cost. 

For the northeastern states and hilly regions, the subsidy is increased to 60 percent. 

The maximum project cost eligible for subsidy is capped at INR 1 crore. 

Thus, the maximum subsidy amount for a 30-ton ice plant or cold storage facility can be INR 40 lakh. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of technology in the fisheries sector. 

It encourages the adoption of modern techniques for fish preservation and storage. 

The expected outcome is an increase in fish production by 70 lakh tons by 2024-2025. 

The scheme is expected to generate approximately 15 lakh direct and indirect jobs in the fisheries sector. 

Eligibility for this scheme includes both individual and group applicants. 

Individual applicants must be at least 18 years old. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required for applicants. 

However, applicants must demonstrate a genuine interest in the fisheries sector. 

For groups, a minimum of five members is required to form a cooperative society. 

The income criteria for eligibility are not explicitly defined. 

However, applicants must show that they have the financial capacity to invest in the project. 

The application process for the PMMSY scheme is straightforward. 

Interested applicants must submit their applications to the respective State Fisheries Departments. 

The application must include a detailed project report. 

The project report should outline the proposed facility's capacity and technology. 

It should also include a financial plan detailing the estimated costs. 

Required documents include identity proof, address proof, and bank account details. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the State Fisheries Department. 

If approved, the project will be sanctioned, and the subsidy will be disbursed. 

The disbursement of the subsidy is typically done in installments. 

The first installment is released after the project is sanctioned. 

Subsequent installments are released based on the progress of the project. 

The timeline for project completion is generally set at 12 months from the date of sanction. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Department of Fisheries under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry, and Dairying. 

The contact details for the Department of Fisheries can be found on their official website. 

State Fisheries Departments in Haryana will also have specific contact points for queries. 

The PMMSY scheme is a part of the larger vision of the Government of India to promote sustainable fisheries. 

It aligns with the goal of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

The scheme also aims to improve the livelihoods of fishers and fish farmers. 

It is expected to enhance the overall economic growth of the fisheries sector. 

The initiative is also aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). 

It particularly focuses on Goal 14 which aims to conserve and sustainably use the oceans, seas, and marine resources. 

The PMMSY scheme is a significant step towards achieving self-sufficiency in fish production. 

It also aims to boost exports of fish and fish products from India. 

The scheme is expected to contribute to the overall development of rural areas. 

By providing cold storage and ice facilities, it will help in reducing wastage. 

This will ensure that fish reaches the market in a fresh and consumable state. 

The PMMSY scheme also encourages the use of renewable energy sources. 

It promotes the installation of solar panels for ice plants and cold storage. 

This is aimed at reducing the carbon footprint of the fisheries sector. 

The government also provides training and capacity-building programs for beneficiaries. 

These programs focus on modern fish farming techniques and post-harvest management. 

The PMMSY scheme is a comprehensive initiative that addresses multiple aspects of the fisheries sector. 

It is designed to empower fishers and fish farmers economically. 

The establishment of ice plants and cold storage facilities is a critical component of this empowerment. 

The scheme is expected to bring about a significant transformation in the fisheries landscape of Haryana. 

It will enable better market access for fishers and enhance their bargaining power. 

The PMMSY scheme is a vital tool for achieving sustainable fisheries in India. 

It represents the government's commitment to improving the livelihoods of those in the fisheries sector. 

The scheme is expected to have a lasting impact on the economy of Haryana. 

It will create a more resilient and sustainable fisheries sector in the state. 

The PMMSY scheme is an important part of India's broader agricultural and rural development strategy. 

It aims to ensure food security and nutritional security for the population. 

The establishment of ice plants and cold storage facilities will play a crucial role in this endeavor. 

The PMMSY scheme is a forward-looking initiative that seeks to modernize the fisheries sector. 

It is a significant step towards achieving the goals of the National Fisheries Policy. 

The scheme is expected to lead to increased fish production and better livelihoods for fishers. 

In conclusion, the PMMSY scheme for ice plants and cold storage facilities is a comprehensive initiative. 

It aims to enhance the fisheries sector in Haryana and across India. 

The focus on technology and sustainability makes it a forward-thinking program. 

This initiative is poised to make a significant impact on the livelihoods of fishers and fish farmers.
